evals.expected_output: A Python publishing function that validates the post locally before any API call (text length with emojis counted as UTF-8 bytes, at most 5 links, 2–20 items) and implements the 3-step carousel flow (item containers with is_carousel_item=true -> CAROUSEL container with comma-separated children -> threads_publish), status polling with ERROR/EXPIRED handling and timeout, topic_tag and reply_control=accounts_you_follow on the parent, correct handling of the link (link_attachment is TEXT-only), and permalink lookup by media ID.
expectations: Each carousel item container is created with is_carousel_item=true and an explicit media_type of IMAGE or VIDEO.
The parent container is created with media_type=CAROUSEL and `children` as a comma-separated list of the item container IDs.
Before publishing, the code polls GET /{container-id}?fields=status (with error_message) and only proceeds once the containers (at least the video) report FINISHED.
The code handles a container in ERROR (surfacing error_message), EXPIRED, and a polling timeout without publishing.
topic_tag=攝影展 is sent as the topic_tag parameter and reply_control=accounts_you_follow is set, both on the carousel parent container.
The link is not sent as link_attachment on the carousel, and the reply explains that link preview cards only work on text-only posts (the link stays plain text).
It publishes via POST /{user}/threads_publish with creation_id=<carousel container id>, then fetches the permalink with the returned media ID (GET /{media-id}?fields=permalink) and prints it.
The access token comes from the environment/config (not hard-coded) and requests go to graph.threads.net/v1.0 (or graph.threads.com/v1.0).

Before any API call, the code validates the post locally and creates no container when a check fails: the text length counted the way Threads counts it (at most 500, with each emoji counted as its UTF-8 byte length, e.g. ☕️ = 6), at most 5 unique URLs in the text, and 2–20 carousel items. Counting with plain len(text), or leaving any of the three checks to the API, fails.

evals.prompt:
同事寫的這段 Threads 發文程式上線後問題一堆：發文常常失敗或報錯、篩選純文字貼文永遠回傳空清單、抓數據也一直報錯。幫我 code review，列出每個問題的原因，然後給一份修好的版本。

```python
import os
import requests

TOKEN = os.environ["THREADS_TOKEN"]
BASE = "https://graph.threads.net"


def post_image_with_poll(text, image_url):
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/me/threads", data={
        "media_type": "IMAGE",
        "image_url": image_url,
        "text": text,
        "poll_attachment": {"option_a": "要", "option_b": "不要"},
        "reply_control": "ACCOUNTS_YOU_FOLLOW",
        "access_token": TOKEN,
    })
    container_id = r.json()["id"]
    r = requests.post(f"{BASE}/me/threads_publish",
                      data={"creation_id": container_id, "access_token": TOKEN})
    print("published", r.json())
    return container_id


def text_posts_only():
    r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1.0/me/threads",
                     params={"fields": "id,text,media_type", "access_token": TOKEN})
    return [p for p in r.json()["data"] if p["media_type"] == "TEXT"]


def insights(post_id):
    r = requests.get(f"{BASE}/v1.0/{post_id}/insights",
                     params={"metric": "views,likes", "access_token": TOKEN})
    return r.json()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    pid = post_image_with_poll("新品要不要出大杯？", "https://cdn.example.com/cup.jpg")
    print(insights(pid))
    print(len(text_posts_only()))
```
evals.expected_output: A review naming each defect with its cause, and a corrected version: /v1.0 on every call, poll is TEXT-only and a JSON string (resolve the IMAGE+poll conflict openly), lowercase reply_control, wait for FINISHED before publishing, compare against TEXT_POST and paginate, insights by media ID not container ID, real error handling.
expectations: Flags that /me/threads and /me/threads_publish are called without the /v1.0 version segment and fixes the base URL.

Flags that poll_attachment only works on TEXT posts, so an IMAGE post with a poll cannot work, and resolves this openly (e.g. separate text post with the poll, or ask which feature to keep) rather than silently dropping the poll or the image.
Flags that poll_attachment must be sent as a JSON-encoded string (json.dumps), not a Python dict in form data.
Flags that reply_control takes lowercase values when creating (accounts_you_follow); the UPPER_CASE form is only what reply_audience returns when reading.
Adds polling of the container status (GET /{container-id}?fields=status,error_message) until FINISHED before calling threads_publish, with handling of ERROR/EXPIRED/timeout.

Explains that read results use media_type TEXT_POST (not TEXT), so the filter must compare against TEXT_POST, and that the list must be paginated with paging.cursors.after instead of reading only the first page: the fix builds each next request itself with after=<cursor> and stops when there is no after cursor or data comes back empty. A loop that continues only while paging.next is present fails, because the docs say list responses carry no next URL (following next when it does appear is fine if the loop doesn't depend on it).
Flags that the function returns the container ID, and insights must be requested with the media ID returned by threads_publish.
Replaces the bare r.json()["id"] accesses with error handling that checks the HTTP status and surfaces the Meta error envelope (message, code, fbtrace_id) without logging the token.

evals.prompt:
幫我把下面這篇文字發到 Threads，明天早上 8 點發。如果一則放得下就發一則，放不下就拆成串文（第一則當主文，其餘依序回覆在下面）。token 在環境變數 THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN。

【在家手沖入門：我花三年踩過的坑】☕️

很多人問我在家手沖要從哪裡開始，今天一次整理。

1. 豆子比器材重要。與其花五千買手沖壺，不如先買新鮮烘焙、兩週內的豆子。超市架上的豆子常常已經放了好幾個月，香氣早就跑光了。

2. 磨豆機是唯一值得多花錢的器材。刀片式磨豆機磨出來粗細不均，萃取一定不穩定；入門的手搖錐刀就能大幅改善。

3. 水溫抓 90 到 93 度。淺焙可以高一點，深焙低一點，太燙容易苦。沒有溫度計的話，水滾後靜置一分鐘差不多。

4. 粉水比先用 1:15。15 克豆子配 225 克水，先固定這個比例，再依口味微調，不要一次改好幾個變數。

5. 悶蒸不能省。先倒兩倍粉重的水，等 30 秒讓二氧化碳排出，之後的萃取會均勻很多。

6. 注水穩定比手法花俏重要。網路上各種繞圈法看看就好，先練到水流粗細一致，比什麼都有用。

7. 記錄每一杯。豆子、研磨刻度、水溫、時間、味道，寫下來才知道是哪個變數造成差異。我的筆記本現在已經寫到第四本了 📒

最後，好喝最重要。規則是拿來打破的，找到你自己喜歡的那一杯，才是手沖最好玩的地方 😊

你們在家都怎麼沖？留言分享一下吧 👇

Chains the thread correctly: publishes the first part, then each next part as a reply with reply_to_id set to the previous part's (or the root's) media ID returned by threads_publish, not a container ID.

States that the Threads API has no native scheduling, so the 8 AM post must be triggered by something that runs then (the user's cron/Task Scheduler/a scheduled job, or posting at that time), and does not create containers now for publishing tomorrow (or notes containers expire after 24 h).
Checks for THREADS_ACCESS_TOKEN, reports that it is not available in this environment, and asks the user to set or provide it (or hands over a ready-to-run command for their machine).

Shows the exact content of every part and the parameters to be sent in the reply itself and asks for explicit confirmation before anything is published; nothing is published and the reply does not claim a post was made or scheduled.

Before publishing, it verifies the target account (GET /me?fields=id,username), shows the user which account the thread will be posted to, and stops for the user's explicit OK before it starts waiting for 8 AM or registers a scheduled job (e.g. the assistant asks after the check, or the script prompts and waits for an answer). Printing the account and carrying on, with Ctrl+C as the only way to stop, fails.

Before publishing, the flow checks the publishing quota with GET /me/threads_publishing_limit (quota_usage and config) and posts nothing when quota_usage has reached quota_total, since the API has no native scheduling and the app must enforce the 250-posts/24 h quota itself.
